instruction: Navigate to the Privacy & Security settings in Thunderbird. Open the security configuration page within the Settings tab.

metadata.explanation: Task requires opening Settings and then navigating to Privacy & Security section. Slightly more complex than original as it requires multiple steps. Uses accessibility tree to verify both Settings tab is open and Privacy & Security label is visible.
metadata.similarity_to_original: high - same app, similar interaction pattern (navigate to page), slightly more complex

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator checks for Settings tab and Privacy & Security label presence, which covers basic requirements
Missing postconfig to ensure UI state is preserved/reopened after task completion - evaluator may read stale state if user navigates away
Incomplete verification: only checks that Privacy & Security label exists, not that the actual security configuration PAGE is opened and displayed
Evaluator might pass if menu item is visible but page content is not actually shown - potential false positive
Getter (accessibility_tree) is appropriate for UI verification
Metric logic (check_accessibility_tree) correctly validates presence of elements with CSS selectors
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add postconfig to reopen Settings tab and navigate to Privacy & Security section before evaluation
Enhance selectors to verify actual page content is displayed (e.g., check for specific security setting controls/panels within Privacy & Security page, not just the navigation label)
Consider adding a third rule to check for a distinctive element within the Privacy & Security page content area to confirm the page is actually open
Example improved selector: check for specific security configuration panels or settings that only appear when the page is truly opened
